prompt: You want a model where the log of variance is modeled, so the variance stays positive whatever the parameter signs.
why: EGARCH models ln σ², removing positivity constraints.

prompt: The model has separate terms for the size |zₜ₋₁| and the sign zₜ₋₁ of the standardized shock.
why: EGARCH's θz + γ(|z| − E|z|) structure separates sign and size.
trap: GJR uses an indicator on squared shocks instead.

prompt: Constrained GARCH fits keep hitting parameter bounds, and you want asymmetry without those constraints.
why: EGARCH needs no positivity constraints and handles asymmetry.
trap: Both handle asymmetry; only one drops constraints.

prompt: In this model, a large shock scales variance multiplicatively rather than adding to it.
why: Modeling the log turns additive effects into multiplicative ones on σ².
trap: That's a structural difference from GARCH and GJR.

prompt: An EGARCH fit returns a significantly negative coefficient on zₜ₋₁ for a stock.
why: Negative θ means negative shocks raise log variance more: the leverage effect, in EGARCH form.
trap: Same economics as GJR, different parameterization.

prompt: You fit GARCH(1,1), GJR and EGARCH to the same index returns; the log-variance model has the lowest AIC and clean diagnostics.
tells: the log-variance model has the lowest AIC
trap: Identify it by its structure, not by name.
